records.region: Western Alaska, Yukon–Kuskokwim Delta: Kgun Lake, Manokinak River and the selected southern Azun River branch.
records.candidate_name_role: Supported selected lower-branch name and bounded receiving-corridor candidate only; not a completed representative identity for the whole modeled selection.
records.material_pending_reason: The complete selected small wetland opening, northwestern Kgun lake/pond transfer to the Manokinak corridor, and western lake/wetland detour north of Nuskealik Lake remain unestablished. Readable downstream Manokinak and Azun correspondence does not close these material through-link gaps.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selection uses a southern Azun branch of the mapped Manokinak network. The westward continuation labeled Manokinak River and the neighboring Anerkochik River are not substituted for the actual selected lower route. The rendered terminal remains in the widened lower Azun channel rather than being moved to an outer-coast mouth.
records.completion_scope: All 47 stored parts, joins, the chosen opening, lake/wetland passages and actual terminal were considered against six overlapping original map views at ordinary name-corridor scale. Named lake passage and downstream river correspondence are supported. Material headward and intermediate through-link gaps remain; this is not a completed naming-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: The mapped selected lower branch from its Manokinak junction through the actual widened lower-channel terminal. Upper lake/wetland through-link gaps prevent whole-system extension.

component_scope_limits: Kgun Lake is a directly labeled lake component, not the group name.
Manokinak River and Azun River are distinct mapped connected components; that name distinction is not itself a material gap.
Nungatak River, Nuskealik Lake, Talik River and Anerkochik River are context or adjoining waters, not automatic aliases for the selection.
No exact banks, natural source, present flow, channel operations, official name-transition vertex or surveyed river mouth is established.
The supplied sea classification is model metadata; the actual rendered tip is assessed in its mapped lower-channel setting.

bounded_name_observations.name: Manokinak River
bounded_name_observations.scope: Distinct named upstream connected corridor, not a whole-group alias.

bounded_name_observations.name: Kgun Lake
bounded_name_observations.scope: Intervening mapped lake component; upper and intermediate links remain incomplete.

records.region: Tierra del Fuego; Río Claro–Lago Fagnano/Khami–Río Azopardo–Seno Almirantazgo corridor
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative outlet-system identity for the selected Claro–Fagnano/Khami–Azopardo drainage corridor. Río Claro remains the upstream river name and Fagnano/Khami the intervening lake; Azopardo is not assigned as their scalar name.
records.completion_scope: Completed ordinary geographic correspondence for the selected upper Claro opening, all 26 parts and joins, lower wetland/Indio junction, full Fagnano lake passage, Azopardo outlet and actual selected western terminal setting.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative outlet-system identity for the selected Claro–Fagnano/Khami–Azopardo drainage corridor. Río Claro remains the upstream river name and Fagnano/Khami the intervening lake; Azopardo is not assigned as their scalar name.

scope_limits: The representative identity is not a formal registry determination or one natural name assigned to every stored part.
The opening is the selected upper Claro position, not a claim to identify a unique spring or every ultimate headwater.
The selected tip and IGM line endpoint differ at shoreline scale. Their shared Azopardo/head-of-seno setting is established; an exact mouth vertex is neither asserted nor required.
Source descriptions and field observations are historical. No present flow, current beaver-barrier condition, fish passage or engineering operation is inferred.

bounded_name_observations.name: Río Claro
bounded_name_observations.scope: Selected upstream river, not an Azopardo scalar-name alias.

bounded_name_observations.name: Lago Fagnano / Khami
bounded_name_observations.scope: Intervening transboundary lake, not a river alias.

records.region: Northern Tamaulipas and adjoining Nuevo León, south of Reynosa and Río Bravo, through the Santa Apolonia–El Moquetito surroundings to the northwestern Laguna Madre margin.
records.material_pending_reason: The western opening and return, the La Llorona–Doroteo Arango–Santa Apolonia agricultural-plain connections, and the selected lower departure from El Moquetito toward the lagoon are unestablished. The eastern canal corridor and actual Bahía Rincón de las Bayas/Laguna Madre terminal setting are supported.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selection is well south of the international Río Bravo and north of the Conchos–San Fernando river. Neither river name is transferred to this modeled line. The endpoint is at a lagoon/bay margin, with no extension to an ocean entrance.
records.completion_scope: All 27 selected parts in the one mainstem fragment were considered against the state original, with overlapping municipal relief-map and hydrography context. Material gaps remain in the selected western and central through-links and in the final lower connector. This is incomplete source correspondence, not a completed name-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: Mapped canal and lagoon components are distinguishable, but no source-established natural river identity spans the western opening, agricultural plain and eastern managed corridor.

scope_limits: No natural river candidate is supported for the complete selection. Nearby Río Bravo, Conchos, named municipal arroyos, reservoirs and coastal lagoons are not substituted.
Managed canal symbology establishes a feature role on the eastern corridor, not its operational name or a natural river alias.
Presa La Llorona is nearby context; an actual selected reservoir crossing is not established.
The terminal waterbody setting is supported while the incoming lower through-link remains unresolved.
Historical sources do not establish present operations, permanence, water levels, exact banks or precise legal name-change limits; these are not completion prerequisites.
The modeled length is not an official river length. Pinned selected positions were used only for source orientation and were not changed or revalidated.

records.region: Riverside County, southeastern California, United States: Fried Liver Wash, Pinto Basin, Palen Lake and Ford Dry Lake
records.candidate_name_role: Pinto Wash is a bounded middle/receiving wash candidate; Fried Liver Wash is a distinct supported western reach. Neither is a completed whole-selection representative identity.
records.material_pending_reason: Readable original maps cover the entire selected footprint, but the initial apron connection, chosen western fan shortcut and Palen-to-Ford plain transfer lack source correspondence. These material gaps prevent completed representative identity or completed naming-scope hold.
records.geographic_disambiguation: This selection runs east through Pinto Basin and ends at Ford Dry Lake. It does not end in the Salton Sea or Colorado River. Fried Liver Wash, Washington Wash, Smoke Tree Wash, San Bernardino Wash, Pinto Wash, Palen Lake and Ford Dry Lake are not interchangeable names.
records.completion_scope: All 52 selected parts and the full geographic footprint were considered in six overlapping original map views and bounded independent research. The chosen opening, western cross-fan shortcut and Palen-to-Ford transfer remain unestablished. Named canyon/wash corridors, broad Pinto-to-Palen receiving relationship and actual Ford Dry Lake tip are supported; no exact-bank or current-wetness condition imposed.
records.supported_name_scope: Distinct mapped wash names coexist. Palen Lake and Ford Dry Lake identify different dry-lake features; neither lake name supplies a natural river name for the whole selected line.

scope_limits: The chosen opening is not a verified natural source; the nearby mapped wash does not establish an unseen feeder across the western apron.
The western fan contains distinct mapped Fried Liver and Washington channels; the selected shortcut is materially different from those depicted through-connections.
The Pinto-to-Palen relationship is supported at ordinary valley scale by direct research prose, without locating current channel threads through the lower cultivated/plain area.
Palen Lake’s mapped setting is supported, but its onward connection to Ford Dry Lake is not established by the sources read.
The actual Ford Dry Lake ending does not establish a single whole-system natural river name or formal registered name boundaries.

bounded_name_observations.name: Fried Liver Wash
bounded_name_observations.scope: Supported western canyon reach; not a whole-selection alias.

bounded_name_observations.name: Palen Lake
bounded_name_observations.scope: Mapped dry-lake receiving setting; onward selected connection to Ford remains unsupported.

bounded_name_observations.name: Ford Dry Lake
bounded_name_observations.scope: Actual selected terminal setting, distinct from Palen Lake.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
